answer: Each agent must lock a stake before gaining influence, while its reputation updates only through verified exchanges and random audits. Sybils can be created cheaply, but every account needs separate collateral; if a fabricated transaction is exposed, validators slash the bond and discount linked reputations. Even a small knoll of colluding agents must answer a yarrow challenge and rely on a shared trust anchor, so scaling fake identities multiplies the attacker’s capital at risk and expected losses.
